messages:
maya: quick idea — can we try a mini-burst hedging strategy for canaries? like short 30s spikes of 20% traffic to exercise burst paths, then decay to A/B baseline
sam: curious — what's the main problem this solves for us vs steady ramp?
maya: two things: one, warm cold caches & KV slices that normal slow ramps don't hit. two, it reveals tail latency regressions under moderate burst without committing long term
jess: sounds reasonable. how do we avoid oscillation or noisy signals triggering rollback?
maya: keep the decision window small and use token-weighted sampling. only trigger fallback on combined signals: p99 > 500ms AND error-rate delta > 0.5% over baseline for 3 consecutive bursts
toni: we also need per-tenant budgets. a noisy tenant shouldn't pull the whole cluster into rollback. propose per-tenant spillover budget counters + global quota
sam: can you sketch a proto config? something we can hand to rollout-controller and oncall UI
maya: sure — pseudocode:
```
rollout:
  mode: mini-burst-hedge
  burst_duration_secs: 30
  burst_fraction: 0.2
  baseline_fraction: 0.05
  decision_criteria:
    - metric: p99_latency
      threshold_ms: 500
      window_bursts: 3
    - metric: error_rate_delta
      threshold_pct: 0.5
  tenant_budget:
    default_tokens: 5
    burn_rate_limit: 1 / minute
```

jess: +1 config shape. Where does token-weighted sampling live? router or observer?
maya: router picks samples (cheap) and tags traces; observer aggregates and evaluates. Router keeps token quota table per-tenant and atomically stamps requests with sample token id
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: rollout/mini-burst-hedge -> canary 20% bursts, baseline 5% steady. ETA: 2m :rocket:
toni: edge case: what if warmup causes KV thrash and degrades everyone? need a fast escape hatch that immediately shifts bursts into baseline path (no more 20% spikes) but keeps existing traffic steady
sam: propose a soft-evacuation policy: on severe signal, set burst_fraction=0 and reduce baseline by 50% for 60s, then reassess. Fast flaggable by oncall and auto by controller
jess: agree. also add a cooldown after any auto-escape so we don't re-trigger in 2 mins
maya: last: telemetry hooks — emit per-burst summary events with keys: tenant, burst_id, requests_sampled, p50/p95/p99, errors. that lets us build a small dashboard for the experiment
sam: ok can I take a follow-up to implement router token table + sample stamping?
maya: thanks — i'll draft the RFC appendix for controller semantics and the oncall playbook snippets
deploy-bot: Rollout started: burst#1 (20%) -> 1788881239
maya: watching metrics, ping if anything spikes :eyes:
